verdict: Narrow synthetic gate resists reproduced plan substitution, uncaptured expressions and unexported creation; no general retention-safe deployment or joined cleanup claim.
executed_results: Preserved byte-identical initial gate reproduced retained-resource plan-swap destruction, unexported creation, uncaptured file dependency and raw sensitive-expression logging.

Approved plan is read once, hashed, transferred to a sealed memfd, inspected and applied through the same passed descriptor; mutable pathname swap at the final-check barrier cannot substitute applied bytes.
Kernel seal mask 15 rejected write/shrink/grow/seal modifications with EPERM. Actual cleanup deleted only the victim and preserved the extra retained UUID.
Incomplete resource census, file()/sensitive() expressions, unknown inputs and duplicate keys reject before planning; valid fully exported creation with unknown planned ID succeeds.
Existing positive cleanup, receipt, retained mutation, cooperative fencing and real-process-exit cases still pass.
Current logs omit all stdout/stderr bodies and use owner-only modes without a synthetic-value secret filter. Manager state remains plaintext.
Real journal bridge remains negative evidence: unsupported physical UUID/file mapping rejects and mismatched manager effect cannot acknowledge actual file absence.

evidence_boundaries.manager_kernel: Actual local OpenTofu built-ins, Linux memfd seals and process exits
evidence_boundaries.fault_injection: Two missing/denied-sealing mocks; actual host supports sealing
evidence_boundaries.policy: Fake manual retention/membership journal is not authoritative research state
evidence_boundaries.real_adapter: Negative public journal integration only; positive adapter apply unsupported/unexecuted
evidence_boundaries.documentation: Context7 quota exhausted; primary Linux manuals and Python docs downloaded with hashes

limitations: Sealing freezes plan bytes, not arbitrary provider effects, provider Delete authority, manager state or live configuration; apply remains non-atomic.
Direct CLI, privileged or noncooperating actors remain outside cooperative safety.
Memfds are volatile; recovery needs separately retained approved bytes or trusted outcome investigation.
Only exact JSON fixture whitelist and unindexed built-ins supported; full HCL/provider integration unresolved.
Raw state, inputs and metadata can be sensitive despite restricted/omitted logs; no universal secret detection or erasure.
Fake journal still lacks authoritative roots, ownership/dependency/disposed-identity admissions and complete membership; no automatic fence expiry.
handoff: Next candidate experiment: provider-aware immutable retained bundles, versioned receipts and durable identity-scoped Delete authorization, with forced replacement and real mid-provider interruption.
